newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists accuse Juppe of cheating voters.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists accuse Juppe of cheating voters.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin on Wednesday accused Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who is battling a tide of unpopularity, of cheating voters.
Jospin, in a speech to Socialist parliamentarians in the town of Figeac in southern France, denounced what he called a gulf between the centre-right government's promises and its actions.
"The government has failed. And what is more, it has cheated people and has lost the greater part of the credibility it enjoyed at the outset," Jospin said.

A BVA poll for the weekly Paris-Match showed on Tuesday that Juppe's popularity plummeted in September following a widely-criticised tax-cutting package and against a backdrop of continuing near-record unemployment and poor growth prospects.

The poll said 63 percent had a low opinion of Juppe, up from 55 percent in August and his worst score since February. Juppe took power in May 1995 after conservative Jacques Chirac beat Jospin in a run-off for the presidency.
Jospin expressed surprise at the scale of popular opposition to the tax-cutting plan, in which income tax cuts for the better off were offset by hikes in other taxes that hit everyone.
Jospin urged supporters to set their sights on the next 1998 general election.

He set as priorities the struggle to counter the far-right and anti-immigrant National Front, political opposition to the centre-right government, and the need to draft an alternative policy platform.
He said he favoured France joining a single European currency from 1999.
